correctness.rationale: Fresh enumeration of all 6^6 set maps found exactly 446 order-preserving self-maps, six constants and eight bijective order maps. The eight automorphisms are isolated in the full pointwise order. Replaying the specified deterministic beat reduction independently removed 432 maps, 352 by down-beat and 80 by up-beat moves, leaving exactly constants plus automorphisms; the survivor has no beat points and the constants carry the original X_2 order. Thus each deletion is a strong deformation retract and the asserted core decomposition follows.

evidence: The general self-homotopy classification implies the eight automorphisms are singleton components and all nonhomeomorphisms are together, but it does not imply that the null component retracts to X_2.
Finite-sphere topological-complexity work does not compute self-map-space cores.

value.rationale: The prior component classification leaves open the internal topology of the large null component. Showing that it retracts not to a point but back to the minimal finite sphere itself is a sharp and conceptually significant mapping-space phenomenon, with a complete finite certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite-space computation may contain the same 446-map core reduction.

final_claim: For the canonical six-point finite S^2 model X_2, the 446-point compact-open self-map space strongly deformation retracts to the disjoint union of the six constant maps, ordered as X_2, and eight isolated homeomorphisms; hence the null self-map component has X_2 as its Stong core and weak S^2 type.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed finite-space computation may contain the same 446-map core reduction.
The theorem is specific to X_2 and does not give mapping-space cores for all X_n.
